Use **`FileResponse`**, which asynchronously streams a file as the response.[5] You pass it the file path rather than the file's contents:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse

some_file_path = "large-video-file.mp4"
app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/")
async def main():
    return FileResponse(some_file_path)
```

You can also set `response_class=FileResponse` on the decorator. In this case, you can return the file path directly from your *path operation* function.[5]

Useful arguments include:
- `path` - The file path to the file to stream.[5]
- `media_type` - A string giving the media type.[5] If unset, the filename or path will be used to infer a media type.[5]
- `filename` - If set, this will be included in the response `Content-Disposition`.[5]

File responses will include appropriate `Content-Length`, `Last-Modified` and `ETag` headers.[5]

**Alternative: streaming chunks yourself.** If you declare a `response_class=StreamingResponse` in your *path operation function*, you can use `yield` to send each chunk of data in turn.[1] If you read from a file-like object this way, note that in many cases reading a file or a file-like object would block.[4] To avoid blocking the event loop, you can simply declare the *path operation function* with regular `def` instead of `async def`, that way FastAPI will run it on a threadpool worker[4]. Also, with a real file, it would be important to make sure the file is closed after the work with it is done[4], for example by using a `with` block.

More details:
- https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/custom-response/
- https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/stream-data/
